_readme: Known files over the 500-line convention (CLAUDE.md, 'Code organization: 500-line file convention'), as of 2026-08-12. checkFileLength.mjs fails only if a file NOT listed here crosses 500 lines, or a listed file grows past the line count recorded here. Splitting a file below 500 lines does not require touching this file (the script reports it as a housekeeping notice instead of failing) but delete the entry once it's split. Do not bump a recorded number to silence a GREW violation — split the file, or if truly justified, say why right here.
_note_src_game_Game_ts: 1348->1256->1029 (2026-08-12): three form-(2) composition extractions have now landed — controllers/ForgeActions.ts, controllers/ScreenFlow.ts, and controllers/GameLoop.ts (the fixed-step sim + interpolated render main loop: update/advanceSim/stepSim/advanceOnline/spawnBulletTrails/updateFx/updateCamera/updateHud/pollConfirm, plus the accumulator/predictor/prevFire state that was purely internal to those methods). All three take Game as a narrow GameLoopHost/etc. callback interface (this repo's established host-callback-interface pattern, RunOutcome.ts/EventReactor.ts) and never call back into Game beyond that interface. GameLoop.ts got 17 tests against a real createGameEngine (same convention as controllers/ally.test.ts) plus faked Pixi collaborators; verified live via window.__game headless driving that an actual offline run/tutorial run/pause-freeze/resume/quit sequence produces the right tick counts and phase transitions, zero console errors. What's LEFT in Game.ts is: start()'s screen-callback wiring (~120 lines - inherently belongs in the assembly shell, fragmenting it further would hide the full picture of what connects to what), the constructor, run lifecycle (beginRun/beginTutorialRun/beginArenaDemoRun/finalizeOnlineRun/quitRun/resetRunRenderState - genuinely reads/writes phase/engine/session/meta/scene/roomBuilder in combination, see the same cross-call analysis from the two prior extractions), matchmaking/network glue, and thin host-interface implementations. Recorded as tracked debt; the run-lifecycle boundary specifically is the next real candidate if this gets revisited, not the whole file. 1029->1033 (2026-08-12, same day): +4 lines wiring `hud.onSwapWeapon` (the new idle-weapon-slot HUD chip's tap callback) straight to `builder.requestSwap()`, one line beside the existing `hud.onPause` wiring one line above it — the exact 'screen-callback wiring... inherently belongs in the assembly shell' category already called out above, not new debt shape. 1033->1042 (2026-08-31, unpickable-loot investigation): +9 lines wiring `PickupDebugOverlay` (`scene/PickupDebugOverlay.ts`, new file, gated behind `?pickupDebug=1`) into the constructor's existing query-param block and the existing `GameLoop` deps object literal — same 'screen-callback/query-param wiring belongs in the assembly shell' category, not new debt shape; the overlay's own logic lives entirely in its own file and stays null in every normal session.
_note_src_game_scene_Actor_ts_removed_20: Actor.ts is OFF this baseline as of 2026-08-25: 552 -> 464 lines, back under the 500-line convention, so per CLAUDE.md its entry is deleted rather than renumbered. The 2026-08-25 element-badge pass pushed it to 589 (a GREW violation), and the fix was the split the previous note already nominated rather than a bumped number. TWO extractions landed, in CLAUDE.md's own priority order: (1) `scene/statusAura.ts`, form (1) independent functions — `auraMaskOf` + `drawStatusAura`, a pure drawing function over a caller-owned Graphics with no state of its own, exactly the shape `healthBar.ts` already had; (2) `scene/actorFilters.ts`, form (2) composition — the four lazily-built skin shaders (shield shell / hit outline / death dissolve / burn heat-haze) and the rule that composes them into one `filters` list, taking a ONE-METHOD host interface (`setSkinFilters`) because that is the entire cross-boundary call list, with no call in the other direction. Both are behaviour-preserving: Actor.test.ts's existing filter assertions were kept verbatim (their private-field accessors now reach one level deeper through `fx`) and still pass. Previous note, for history: 500->552 (2026-08-21, two same-day fixes): (a) the health bar moved off this container onto `layers.hud` (live report the wall's occlusion x-ray washes its dark contour/track into the wall's own faded tone) — needed a new `applyTransform`/`destroy` override pair (the exact 'owned but not parented, position synced by hand' shape `Entity.shadow` already uses) plus their doc comments; (b) the HOVER table's 2026-08-19 retune comment only quoted its base-to-peak half, so the follow-up fix got its own paragraph recording what the trough actually was and why every entry's range changed. Both additions are load-bearing doc comments, not padding, and both bug fixes are cheap/surgical on their own — this file was already the second-largest presentation class in the client (skin + weapon + health bar + status auras + four conditional shield/outline/dissolve/heatHaze filters + hover), and splitting it properly deserves its own pass rather than a rushed extraction during two unrelated bug fixes. The filter cluster (`applySkinFilters`/`setShieldActive`/`hitFlash`/`startDissolve`/`isDissolved`, all touching the same four lazily-built filter fields) is the natural form-(2) composition candidate if this gets revisited, same shape as Game.ts's own tracked-debt note above.
